It depends what frame of reference you're talking about population levels. Economically/capitalistically, it is crucial to have an exponentially growing work force in order to grow an economy. But in terms of the health of the planet, sociologically, in terms of resource allocation and the preservation of natural habits, overpopulation is 100% an issue
People's perception of overpopulation can often be driven by the fact that they live in urban areas with very high population density.
It’s real just not in the western world but it soon will be.

There is this crazy assumption that a smaller population would pollute the Earth less. Most pollution actually comes from carelessness and waste, not scale of production. We have the technology today to cleanly support a population of 9 billion. What we don’t have is leaders or an elite class willing to make that happen. A smaller population isn’t going to change the ethos.
Overpopulation is double-speak for "I think I have too many neighbors in my posh community and it's bothering me but I don't want to be labeled the bad guy so I'll just make it everyone's problem"
It's a well known pattern, once a civilization develop so far it stops maintaining itself and collapse
Did Ehrlich do the same as the Club of Rome and just assuming the growth rate will forever be constant instead of declining over time?

If overpopulation was a thing, why is the explosive growth of, for example, Africa's population not addressed? At the current rate, we could probably have no children at all in Europe and North America, and the world population would still grow.
People who complain about overpopulation and global warming are generally ignrants selfish ppl.
